summary: Task 2 vendoring is production-ready. The new chart-4.4.9.min.js is byte-identical to the official Chart.js 4.4.9 UMD min build from jsdelivr (SHA-256 bce154080959c574be0bb6b1a924ff32f08ebc6ff460c159171f51c53802c844, 206944 bytes). All 50 MANIFEST.txt entries (26 JS + 4 CSS + 20 KaTeX webfonts) hash-match their on-disk counterparts. pbxproj correctly left untouched: the existing ditto-based Run Script (line 349) recursively copies the whole vendor/ directory, so chart-4.4.9.min.js will be included in the bundle automatically.

suggestions.suggestion: chart-4.4.9.min.js is the only vendored file that follows the version-in-filename convention (the requested vendoring discipline). All 25 pre-existing JS assets and all 4 CSS assets use unversioned names (mermaid.min.js, katex.min.js, prism.min.js, etc.), with version pinned only inside MANIFEST.txt. Consider a follow-up task to either (a) rename existing assets to match the new convention (e.g., mermaid-10.6.1.min.js), updating index.html script tags accordingly, or (b) explicitly document in MANIFEST.txt that the version-in-filename convention applies only to assets vendored from this commit forward. This is out of scope for Task 2 but worth tracking to avoid drift.
suggestions.benefit: Project-wide consistency makes accidental version mismatches visible at the filesystem level, not just in MANIFEST.txt. Reduces risk of silent upgrades during ad-hoc file replacement.

suggestions.suggestion: MANIFEST.txt does not record the on-disk filename for each entry. For most entries the filename is trivially derivable from the lib_name column (e.g., 'mermaid' -> mermaid.min.js), but for two cases this mapping is non-obvious: 'prismjs-html' -> prism-html.min.js (vendored from upstream prism-markup.min.js, intentional rename because Prism aliases languages.html = languages.markup), and 'katex-auto-render' -> auto-render.min.js. Adding a 7th column 'local_path' (e.g., js/chart-4.4.9.min.js) would let a verification script idempotently re-hash by parsing the manifest, instead of requiring out-of-band knowledge of the rename. The header comment on line 7 already promises 'verified against shasum -a 256 <file> of on-disk file in this directory' — recording the file path would make that promise machine-checkable.
suggestions.benefit: Enables a CI hook (or pre-commit script) to validate manifest integrity automatically: parse manifest -> for each row, shasum the local_path -> diff vs sha256 column. Today this requires a human to know the file-rename mapping.

suggestions.suggestion: Three entries (mermaid 10.6.1, katex 0.16.9, prismjs 1.29.0) carry 'Risk accepted' notes for known CVEs with patched upstream versions available (mermaid 11.x, katex 0.16.21, prismjs 1.30.0). The risk-acceptance rationale (sandboxed WKWebView, no untrusted DOM context, fenced-code-only Prism input) is reasonable and well-documented inline, but the manifest does not link these deferrals to a tracking artifact (issue ID, todo file, scheduled milestone). Consider appending an issue reference to each 'Upgrade ... scheduled separately' note (e.g., 'tracked: issue #NN' or 'tracked: tasks/lessons.md'). Otherwise the deferrals risk becoming permanent.
suggestions.benefit: Makes the upgrade obligation actionable and discoverable. Aligns with the lessons.md / tasks/todo.md workflow described in CLAUDE.md.

verificationEvidence.prism_html_aliasing_confirmed: prism-html.min.js is upstream prism-markup.min.js; Prism source sets Prism.languages.html = Prism.languages.markup
verificationEvidence.manifest_format_consistency: all 50 rows use uniform 6-column pipe-delimited format (lib_name | version | sha256 | source_url | cve_check_date | cve_check_result)
